title: Textured check baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in an eight-row knit-purl check on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in DK worked flat in a large knit-purl check pattern: eight stitches wide by eight rows tall, alternating every repeat. The surface has bold raised squares that read as a windowpane grid. About 255 g of DK.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1889), §Check Patterns, gives a large-block knit-purl check for blankets. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Moss Stitch Variations, discusses the eight-row check as a cot blanket pattern.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in textured check on 4 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern formed by alternating blocks of knit stitches and purl stitches over a repeating grid, then switching their positions after a set number of rows. The knit blocks advance forward (stocking stitch surface) while the purl blocks recede (reverse stocking stitch), creating a reversible checkerboard of raised and recessed squares.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles in a large-block
knit-purl check
pattern, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The eight-stitch, eight-row check was chosen because the blocks are large enough to read clearly as a bold grid from arm's length. The check lies flat because the knit and purl blocks balance across both dimensions. The pattern requires only knit and purl: no cables, yarn-overs, or slip stitches. Budget about 255 g (about 560 m / 615 yards) of machine-washable DK. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 255 g (about 560 m / 615 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm over textured check on 4 mm needles, unblocked. Swatch the full 16-row block sequence (8 rows set A + 8 rows set B) for at least 15 cm.
At 20 stitches per 10 cm with 168 stitches, the blanket will be about 84 cm wide rather than 75 cm.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 168 stitches (a multiple of 8 for the check repeat). Long-tail tail: (4 × 168) / 10 + 15 = 67.2 + 15 = 82 cm. Measure 95 cm.
Body (16-row complete repeat)
Rows 1 to 8 (set A): RS rows: *k8, p8; rep from * to end. WS rows: *k8, p8; rep from * to end (the WS row works the same as the RS, maintaining the column alignment).
Rows 9 to 16 (set B): RS rows: *p8, k8; rep from * to end. WS rows: *p8, k8; rep from * to end.
Repeat the 16-row complete cycle until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note which of the 16 rows you are on.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 135 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 168 stitches, a multiple of 8. At row 268 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Block sequence shifting: set A and set B were swapped at the wrong row, producing a diagonal rather than a rectangular check. Count carefully within the 16-row cycle; a row counter is helpful.
Purl bumps showing in knit sections on the WS: the WS row was worked with knit and purl transposed. Read the stitch on the needle: a knit stitch looks like a V; purling a V stitch is the error.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern (k the knit stitches, p the purl stitches) with a relaxed tension, ending on the final row of a complete set.
Finishing
Weave in both ends along a knit row on the wrong side. The check pattern is reversible; either face can be the front.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From a plain check, a natural progression is a coloured check: two DK colours alternating every eight rows, keeping the same knit-purl check within each colour section. The colour sequences produce the illusion of a woven fabric.
